```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
hc_set_theme("hcrt", tooltip = list(valueDecimals = 2))
old_bootstrap_theme <- shiny::getShinyOption("bootstrapTheme")
shiny::shinyOptions(bootstrapTheme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5))
```

## A chart that reacts to an input

Put `highchartOutput()` in the interface and assign a `renderHighchart()`
expression in the server. Inputs used by that expression trigger a new chart.
The application below switches between sepal and petal measurements for the
same 150 iris flowers. Its theme matches the documentation site.

## Run it in R or in your browser

The tabs keep the live application and its complete source together. The
browser version uses Shinylive and downloads its R runtime and packages on
first launch, which can take a moment. It runs without a hosted Shiny server.
The browser app uses the release available in webR; running the source locally
uses your installed highcharter version.

```{r shiny-tabs, echo=FALSE}
app <- paste(readLines(here::here("dev", "shiny", "site-demo", "app.R")), collapse = "\n")
bslib::navset_card_tab(
  bslib::nav_panel("Browser app",
    htmltools::tags$iframe(src = "../live/index.html", title = "Interactive iris chart in Shinylive",
                          loading = "lazy", style = "width:100%;height:510px;border:0;")),
  bslib::nav_panel("App source", htmltools::tags$pre(htmltools::tags$code(app))),
  bslib::nav_panel("Run locally",
    htmltools::tags$p("From the repository root, run:"),
    htmltools::tags$pre(htmltools::tags$code('shiny::runApp("dev/shiny/site-demo")')))
)
```

## Update an existing chart with a proxy

A proxy changes a chart already on the page. This is useful when you want to
preserve its current zoom or avoid rebuilding a large widget. Give each series
an ID so updates do not depend on its position in the series list.

```{r proxy-recipe, eval=FALSE}
proxy <- highchartProxy("prices", session)
hcpxy_set_data(proxy, data = replacement, idSeries = "closing")
hcpxy_set_extremes(proxy, min = base::as.Date("2025-01-03"), max = base::as.Date("2025-01-08"))
```

The [Stock article](stock.html#update-a-series-and-its-visible-range-in-shiny)
has the full proxy application. It changes both the data and visible date range
while preserving the mounted chart.

The [highcharter-shiny repository](https://github.com/jbkunst/highcharter-shiny)
collects further examples of events, linked views and time-series applications.
For Bootstrap color modes, see the [themes article](themes.html).

```{r restore-bootstrap, include=FALSE}
shiny::shinyOptions(bootstrapTheme = old_bootstrap_theme)
```
